card.title: Short Story 2 — The Oval Portrait (Edgar Allan Poe)

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: ## The story at a glance "The Oval Portrait" by Edgar Allan Poe is Gothic horror in miniature — two short paragraphs of frame and one page of tale inside it — and it contains one of literature's cruellest ideas: a portrait so lifelike that the life it took is visible in it.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Two-layer memory hook: outer layer = narrator and chateau, inner layer = painter and bride. Say which layer you are writing about.
MCQ trap: an option saying the wife died of illness is wrong; the cause is the painting absorbing her life.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: If short of time, give the setting in three words: abandoned chateau, Apennines.  ·  Name the author and the genre, a short story with Gothic elements, at the start of a short answer.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Do not invent events beyond the notes; the painter's account is reached through a note read by the narrator.  ·  Describe the frame narrative technique used in the story.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Summarize 'The Oval Portrait' in 100 words.  ·  What are the Gothic elements in Poe's story?

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Why is the painter's relationship with his bride described as destructive?  ·  ## The characters worth an essay **The painter** is obsession given a brush: he loves his art more than his wife, and Poe is careful to make him neither cruel nor careless — he is simply blind, "wrapt" in his work, seeing only the canvas while the life he is copying drains beside him. That blindness, not malice, is what makes the story frightening: destruction by devotion.…

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## The plot and its frame, retold with an eye on structure The story is built as a **frame narrative** — a story inside a story — and the frame is doing quiet work. The wounded narrator and his servant Pedro break into a chateau rich with artistic treasures but heavy with decay: cobwebs, trophies, black curtains.…  ·  ## The devices, with evidence - **Frame narrative** — the outer story (narrator, chateau, candle) encloses the inner tale (painter, wife, death); the frame distances the horror and makes the inner story feel like evidence rather than invention.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Symbol chain to recall: the painting absorbs life, the wife grows pale, she dies, and the art lives forever.  ·  Device keyword test: 'hints' = foreshadowing, 'vessel' = symbolism, 'greatest work costs a life' = irony.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Discuss the theme of art versus life.  ·  Explain the symbolism of the oval frame.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## The themes worth an essay **Art versus life** — the central theme: creation that feeds on its subject, beauty achieved at the cost of the living. **Obsession** — the painter's single-mindedness as a force that blinds; the story is a study in how passion justifies destruction.…  ·  ## How NEB asks it **"What did the narrator find in the book?" (4 marks)** — the entry on the oval portrait: the painter, his bride, the weeks of work, the death.
